anton-rubinstein.text: Theodore Thomas led 12 of his 13 performances in the 1880s, but others kept playing him after that. He faded over decades, not at one moment; the sparkline shows the slope.

henry-kimball-hadley.text: He mostly conducted his own music: 96 of his 109 performances in the 1920s were under his own baton. After he last conducted his music, in 1932-33, everyone else together played him 10 times in the next ten seasons. One piece carried him: Culprit Fay Rhapsody, Op. 62, 57 of the 109.
henry-kimball-hadley.note: Hadley was the Philharmonic’s associate conductor from 1921 to 1927, the first American to hold a full-time post with a major American orchestra.

william-schuman.text: Leonard Bernstein, music director from 1958 to 1969, led 39 of his 84 performances in the 1960s. After Leonard Bernstein last led his music, in 1985-86, everyone else together played him 24 times in the next ten seasons.

karl-goldmark.text: Josef Stransky, music director from 1911 to 1923, led 46 of his 50 performances in the 1910s. After Josef Stransky last led his music, in 1919-20, everyone else together played him 18 times in the next ten seasons.

mikhail-ippolitov-ivanov.text: 24 of his 55 performances in the 1920s were summer Stadium concerts, under 7 conductors. He faded over decades, not at one moment; the sparkline shows the slope. One piece carried him: Caucasian Sketches, Suite No. 1, 55 of the 55.

ernest-schelling.text: Willem Mengelberg, music director from 1922 to 1928, led 28 of his 53 performances in the 1920s. After Willem Mengelberg last led his music, in 1927-28, everyone else together played him 21 times in the next ten seasons. One piece carried him: A Victory Ball, 30 of the 53.
ernest-schelling.note: Schelling was the first conductor of the Philharmonic’s Young People’s Concerts, which began in March 1924.

frederick-delius.text: John Barbirolli, music director from 1936 to 1941, led 22 of his 48 performances in the 1930s. After John Barbirolli last led his music, in 1962-63, everyone else together played him 15 times in the next ten seasons.

jaromir-weinberger.text: John Barbirolli, music director from 1936 to 1941, led 23 of his 39 performances in the 1930s. After John Barbirolli last led his music, in 1942-43, everyone else together played him 10 times in the next ten seasons. One piece carried him: Schwanda the Bagpiper, 21 of the 39.
jaromir-weinberger.note: Schwanda the Bagpiper was a hit on stages worldwide. Weinberger, born into a Jewish family in Prague, fled the Nazis for the US in 1939; none of his later works matched it.

hugo-wolf.text: Josef Stransky, music director from 1911 to 1923, led 9 of his 22 performances in the 1910s. After Josef Stransky last led his music, in 1916-17, everyone else together played him 3 times in the next ten seasons.

rubin-goldmark.text: Willem Mengelberg, music director from 1922 to 1928, led 21 of his 34 performances in the 1920s. After Willem Mengelberg last led his music, in 1927-28, everyone else together played him 9 times in the next ten seasons. One piece carried him: A Negro Rhapsody, 24 of the 34.

george-whitefield-chadwick.text: Josef Stransky, music director from 1911 to 1923, led 17 of his 21 performances in the 1910s. After Josef Stransky last led his music, in 1922-23, everyone else together played him 5 times in the next ten seasons. One piece carried him: Tam O’Shanter, 11 of the 21.

josef-stransky.text: He mostly conducted his own music: 21 of his 21 performances in the 1910s were under his own baton. After he last conducted his music, in 1920-21, nobody played him for ten seasons.

edward-a-macdowell.text: Ernest Schelling led 16 of his 33 performances in the 1920s. After Ernest Schelling last led his music, in 1936-37, everyone else together played him 12 times in the next ten seasons.

morton-gould.text: No single champion: 12 conductors shared his 37 performances in the 1940s. He faded over decades, not at one moment; the sparkline shows the slope.

max-reger.text: Josef Stransky, music director from 1911 to 1923, led 29 of his 29 performances in the 1910s. After Josef Stransky last led his music, in 1922-23, everyone else together played him 9 times in the next ten seasons.

gustave-charpentier.text: Josef Stransky led 19 of his 19 performances in the 1910s, but others kept playing him after that. He faded over decades, not at one moment; the sparkline shows the slope. One piece carried him: Louise, 16 of the 19.

sigmund-romberg.text: He mostly conducted his own music: 32 of his 38 performances in the 1940s were under his own baton. After he last conducted his music, in 1950-51, everyone else together played him 3 times in the next ten seasons.
